name: SchemaFirst UTM Standard
summary: Deterministic rules for generating UTM parameters. Given the same campaign, source, and distribution context, two conforming agents generate the same UTM.
principle: Same context + same standard = same UTM.

definitions.campaign: The approved campaign identity. An object with `slug` (preferred) and/or `name`.
definitions.source: A canonical source or alias from `sources`, e.g. `linkedin`.
definitions.distribution-context: How the asset is distributed for that source, e.g. `organic`, `paid`, `owned`, `display`. Must be one of that source's `contexts`.
definitions.destination-url: The absolute URL the tracking parameters are appended to.

parameters.name: utm_source
parameters.google-meaning: The referrer of the traffic, such as a search engine, newsletter, or other source.

parameters.name: utm_medium
parameters.google-meaning: The marketing medium, such as cpc, banner, or email newsletter.

parameters.name: utm_campaign
parameters.derivation: `campaign.slug` exactly if present; otherwise the campaign slug algorithm applied to `campaign.name`.
parameters.google-meaning: The name of the campaign, product, promotion, or other identifier.

parameters.name: utm_id
parameters.derivation: The campaign ID from the system of record, passed through unchanged.
parameters.google-meaning: The campaign ID used to identify a specific campaign or promotion.

parameters.name: utm_source_platform
parameters.derivation: The buying or management platform directing the traffic, when one exists. Normalized with the value format rule.
parameters.google-meaning: The platform responsible for directing traffic to a given property, such as a buying platform that sets budgets and targeting criteria.
parameters.applies-when: A buying or management platform directs the traffic.

parameters.name: utm_content
parameters.derivation: The creative or asset identifier, normalized with the value format rule.
parameters.google-meaning: Used to differentiate ads or links that point to the same URL.

parameters.name: utm_term
parameters.derivation: The paid keyword or targeting term, normalized with the value format rule.

parameters.name: utm_creative_format
parameters.derivation: The creative format, normalized with the value format rule.
parameters.google-meaning: The type of creative, such as display, native, video, or search.

parameters.name: utm_marketing_tactic
parameters.derivation: The targeting criteria or tactic, normalized with the value format rule.
parameters.google-meaning: The targeting criteria applied to a campaign, such as remarketing or prospecting.

campaign-naming.rule: utm_campaign represents campaign identity. It is not a container for every available marketing dimension.
precedence: If `campaign.slug` exists, use it exactly. Do not re-normalize it.
Otherwise derive the slug from `campaign.name` with the slug algorithm.
If neither exists, return `requires-context` with `campaign` in `missing`.
slug-algorithm: Apply Unicode NFKD normalization and remove combining marks.
Replace every run of characters outside a-z and 0-9 with a single underscore.

value-format.rule: Apply the campaign slug algorithm. Organization-owned identifiers in utm_id are passed through unchanged.

rules: Remove any existing utm_* parameters from the destination URL.
Preserve all other existing query parameters in their original order.
Append UTM parameters after existing parameters in `parameter-order`.
Omit parameters that have no value. Never emit an empty parameter.
Percent-encode values per RFC 3986. Conforming values require no encoding.
Preserve the URL fragment after the query string.

steps: Resolve `source` to an entry in `sources` by exact match on `canonical-source` or `aliases`, case-insensitive.
Set utm_source and utm_medium from that source.
Set utm_campaign from campaign naming precedence.
Set recommended and optional parameters only from supplied inputs. Never invent values.
Apply the organization profile, if any.

missing-context.behavior: Do not guess. Return a requires-context response listing every missing required input.

unknown-source.behavior: Do not invent a source. Return an unknown-source response.

unsupported-context.behavior: Do not substitute a different context. Return an unsupported-context response listing supported contexts.

provenance-classes.google-defined: Semantics, supported parameters, channel behavior, and documented recommendations from Google Analytics.
provenance-classes.schemafirst-default: Canonical implementation decisions made by SchemaFirst for deterministic agent generation. Not authored or endorsed by Google.
provenance-classes.organization-defined: Values supplied by the adopting organization through an explicit organization profile. Whether a default may be replaced is stated by each parameter's `overridable`.

organization-profile.precedence: Organization profile > SchemaFirst default. Google-defined parameter semantics cannot be overridden.
permitted: Define where organization-owned values come from.
not-permitted: Redefine the meaning of Google-defined UTM parameters.
Remove a parameter from the minimum conforming set.

non-breaking: Adding a distribution context to a source

notes: When Google Ads auto-tagging (GCLID) is enabled, Google Analytics uses auto-tagged values for source and medium. Manual UTMs remain useful for utm_campaign and for traffic where GCLID cannot be used.
Organic search results are not manually tagged.

provenance.explanation: Google documents `google` / `cpc` as the source / medium for paid search, and lists `display` as a Display channel medium.

paid.description: Paid search ads on Microsoft Advertising.

notes: Organic search results are not manually tagged.

provenance.explanation: Google lists Bing as a search site and classifies search-site traffic with a paid medium (matching ^(.*cp.*|ppc|retargeting|paid.*)$) as Paid Search. SchemaFirst selects `bing` as the canonical value.

organic.description: Unpaid posts from company pages or employee profiles.

provenance.explanation: Google lists `social` as an Organic Social medium and classifies social-site traffic with a medium matching paid.* as Paid Social. SchemaFirst selects `paid_social` as the canonical paid medium; Google uses it as an example in its UTM best practices.

organic.description: Unpaid posts from Facebook pages, groups, or profiles.

paid.description: Facebook ads purchased through Meta Ads.

notes: Facebook and Instagram are separate sources even when bought through the same Meta Ads account, following Google's guidance to use one distinct source per sub-platform.

provenance.explanation: Google's best practices give `fb` as an example source. SchemaFirst selects the unabbreviated `facebook` as canonical and registers `fb` as an alias.

organic.description: Unpaid posts, stories, reels, and bio links.

paid.description: Instagram ads purchased through Meta Ads.

notes: Instagram and Facebook are separate sources even when bought through the same Meta Ads account.

provenance.explanation: Google's best practices give `insta` as an example source. SchemaFirst selects the unabbreviated `instagram` as canonical and registers `insta` and `ig` as aliases.
Follows the same social mapping as other social platforms.

organic.description: Links in video descriptions, channel pages, comments, and community posts.

paid.description: YouTube ads not auto-tagged by Google Ads.

notes: YouTube ads bought through Google Ads with auto-tagging are classified by Google Analytics from the ad network type, not from UTMs.
Google evaluates social channels before video channels. Final classification depends on Google's maintained source-category list.

provenance.explanation: Google classifies video-site traffic with a paid medium as Paid Video and traffic with a medium matching ^(.*video.*)$ as Organic Video. SchemaFirst selects `video` and `paid_video`.

owned.description: Email sent to the organization's own lists, including newsletters, nurture, and transactional email.

notes: Organizations that need to distinguish lists or senders should define proprietary sources in an organization profile rather than changing utm_medium.
Use utm_content to distinguish links within the same email.

provenance.explanation: Google classifies traffic as Email when source or medium is email, e-mail, e_mail, or e mail. SchemaFirst selects `email` for both.

owned.description: Text messages sent to the organization's own subscribers.

provenance.explanation: Google classifies traffic as SMS when source or medium exactly matches `sms`.
